..

Tonight to Tuesday morning: high pressure will begin to lose its 
influence over the region as low pressure off the OR/CA coast 
begins to encroach on the area. Look for variable high clouds 
tonight and early Tuesday, but weather will be mostly dry except
for some light rains starting into the Cascade crest Tuesday 
morning. Low tonight will be mostly in the 40s, with a few lower
50s. Highs will be in the 70s.

Tuesday afternoon to Thursday: Low pressure and moistening
deformation axis lifts into the region. This will bring 
increasing rain and thunderstorms chances Tuesday afternoon and 
evening, becoming more likely overnight through Wednesday over a
good portion of the area. The lowest PoPs right now are near 
the Cascades, but this will need to be monitored should the 
moisture wrap farther west with the deformation axis. Those 
steadier rain chance come in from southern WA/lower ID Panhandle
Tuesday overnight and become likely throughout much region 
during the day Wednesday. The deformation axis will be a focal 
point for some moderate to heavy precipitation risk, before the 
low starts to pull east and the deformation axis weakens 
Wednesday night into Thursday. So that will allow the higher 
PoPs to retreat to Idaho and southeast WA Wednesday evening, 
then linger over ID Thursday especially near the ID/MT border. 
Some chance will also linger over the eastern third of WA; then 
PoPs decline into Thursday night. This will be mainly a rain 
event, with the primary snow risk in the higher mountains. Some 
light snow may fall around Lookout Pass by Thursday, but the 
amounts will be low, if any.

Additionally, the chance for thunderstorms comes Tuesday and 
Wednesday. With the leading edge of the upper trough bringing 
some modest diffluent flow entering, the milder air ahead of it 
and a front moving in. This includes a risk for some
nocturnal/overnight t-storms overnight Tuesday into Wednesday 
morning. How widespread these are will be linked to how much the
best lift and instability can sync up. However all areas will 
see at least some risk through Tuesday afternoon into Wednesday 
morning, with the first chances near the Cascades and developing
elsewhere between Tuesday night and Wednesday morning. Some 
could be locally strong. The main risk will be gusty winds and 
hail.

Rain amounts between 0.75 to 1.0" are in the forecast for
Tuesday night into Wednesday night the east third of WA and 
the ID Panhandle, locally between 1.0-1.50" near the higher 
Palouse into the Panhandle mountains. Central WA could seen 
between 0.15 to 0.50 inches. While the Cascades through the 
Okanogan Valley could see between 0.05 to 0.25", highest in the 
mountains. With milder temperatures ahead of this and then the 
rain, this comes with some rises in area rivers. Most mainstem 
river remain below action stage, save for Stehekin which is 
expected to push above minor flood stage Tuesday into Wednesday 
and the Kootenai River at Bonners Ferry may push above action 
stage later in the week. Streams and creeks and poor drainage 
areas and fields will be monitored for flooding as well, with 
areas such as southeast WA including the Palouse prone to 
potential issues as it has had this spring. The best risk will 
be around Wednesday, receding into Thursday.

Look for some breezy conditions, starting Tuesday and continuing 
into Thursday. The stronger winds are forecast Wednesday, with 
gusts in the 15 to 25 mph range, highest near the Cascades to 
Upper Columbia Basin. Locally higher winds are forecast around 
the higher terrain near the Cascades and Blues, with gusts near 
40 mph possible, especially Wednesday. 

Friday to Monday the precipitation potential wanes. Some shower
chances linger around mountain zones for the afternoon hours. 
Otherwise it looks drier. 

As for temperatures, highs drop about 15 degrees heading into
Wednesday compared to Tuesday with readings in the upper 50s 
and 60s. Lows will be the 40s to low 50s Wednesday morning, then
upper 30s and 40s Thursday and Friday morning. /Solveig
